Community ponds are the quickest to warm up after ice out, creating a fair to good pre-spawn largemouth bass and crappie bite.
Black Crappie – Fair: Catch early season crappie in the community ponds slowly retrieving small twister tails or swim baits. If it exists in the pond target edges of cattail stands and any wood habitat.
Largemouth Bass – Good: Catch pre-spawn largemouth bass slowly retrieving plastics and shallow diving crankbaits.

Black Crappie – Fair: Some crappie have started to move shallow to spawn; others are hanging on rock bluffs and brush piles.
Largemouth Bass – Fair: Try fishing shallow areas on warm days.
White Crappie – Good: Some crappies have started to move shallow to spawn; others are hanging on rock bluffs and brush piles.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Crystal Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black Crappie – Fair: Crappie will move shallow as the water warms; use small jigs and live bait.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Green Valley Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Fair: Catch crappie up to 10-inches with jigs or twister tails fished along rocky shorelines.
Largemouth Bass – Fair: Use finesse plastics or crankbaits along rocky shorelines to catch all sizes of largemouth bass.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Hickory Grove Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black Crappie – Fair: Catch crappies shallow casting plastics or live minnows under a bobber near riprap and treefalls throughout the lake.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lake Belva Deer fishing report
reports.text: Black Crappie – Fair: Find crappies in the trees in 10 to 12 feet of water; they aren’t in a rush to spawn.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lake Darling fishing report
reports.text: Black Crappie – Slow: Crappies don’t like the muddy water. They have not started their spawning run. Find one group in 6-7 feet of water and another in 8-10 feet over the habitat.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lake Geode fishing report
reports.text: Black Crappie – Fair: Crappies are a little on the small size yet; they are holding out in a little deeper water waiting for calmer weather for their first spawn.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lake Hendricks fishing report
reports.text: Black Crappie – Fair: Find crappie near woody debris; use a small jib tipped with a minnow under a bobber.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lake Macbride fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Fair: Some fish are on trees in 10-20 feet of water; some are starting to investigate shallower flats.
Largemouth Bass – Fair.
Spotted bass – Fair: They are starting to make nests.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lake Meyer fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Fair: Try fishing in deeper water just off drop-offs or the edge of vegetation.
Largemouth Bass – Slow: Bass are moving to warmer water in the evening. Use a crankbait with a slow retrieve.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lake Miami fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – Slow: Use jigs or plastics in brush piles and submerged habitat.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lake Sugema fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – Slow: Try plastics or spinnerbaits along rocky shorelines.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Little River Watershed Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black Crappie – Fair: Use small jigs or twister tails near rocky shorelines to catch all sizes of crappie.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Lost Grove Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Fair: Find most crappie in mid-depth waters; they are staying out of the shallow for now.
Largemouth Bass – Fair: Bass are starting to get a little more active and aggressive on nicer afternoons. Try fishing the bays on the north side where they are in the warmer water.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Maquoketa River (above Monticello) fishing report
reports.text:
Reports of walleye and black crappie being caught; try fishing below the Lake Delhi Dam and the Manchester whitewater park.
Black Crappie – Fair: Find woody structure on the river around Manchester. Try vertical jigging a lead head jig tipped with a colored tube jig.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 10 fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Slow: Use light tackle and small plastic baits in the flooded timber as the river rises.
Largemouth Bass – Fair: Try fishing the upper portions of backwaters away from current.
Smallmouth Bass – Excellent: Smallmouth are biting in areas with moderate current. Cast spinners and crankbaits along the main channel rock shorelines or at the spillway.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 11 fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Slow: Use light tackle and small plastic baits in the flooded timber as the river rises.
Largemouth Bass – Fair: Try fishing the upper portions of backwaters away from current.
Smallmouth Bass – Excellent: Smallmouth are biting in areas with moderate current. Cast spinners and crankbaits along the main channel rock shorelines.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 12 fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Good: Anglers are catching a few black crappie on wood in deeper backwater lakes. The bite picked up the past few weeks as they think about spawning.
Largemouth Bass – Good: Bass fishing has taken off with anglers concentrating near backwater shorelines as they prepare to spawn.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 14 fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Good: Find wood in deeper backwater lakes. Bite should return when the water warms.
Largemouth Bass – Excellent: Bass have moved along the shorelines in backwater areas; they are easily targeted with a variety of lures and natural baits.
Smallmouth Bass – Good: Look for feeding smallmouth on rocky habitats with good flows. Wing-dams and day markers provide excellent habitat.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 16 fishing report
reports.text:
Largemouth Bass – No Report: Look for bass up shallow in the backwaters around brush piles in Sunset Marina and the Andalusia Island complex.
White Crappie – No Report: Look for crappies to move up shallow. Try jigs and minnows or minnows under a bobber in brush piles at Sunset Marina and the Andalusia Island complex.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 18 fishing report
reports.text:
Largemouth Bass – No Report: Look for bass to move up shallow around brush and logs as water temperatures rise; trying fishing at Huron Island.
White Crappie – No Report: Look for crappies to move up shallow. Try jigs and minnows or minnows under a bobber in brush piles at the Huron Island complex.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 19 fishing report
reports.text:
Largemouth Bass – No Report: Look for bass up shallow in the backwaters around brush piles and logs.
White Crappie – No Report: Look for crappies in the backwaters. Try jigs and minnows or minnows under a bobber in brush piles. Mississippi River levels are forecast to rise over the weekend. Main channel water temperature is 61-63 degrees. Water clarity is fair. Look for crappies to move up shallow in the backwaters. If you have questions on fishing Pools 16-19 contact the Fairport Fish Hatchery at 563-263-5062.

reports.title: Mississippi River Pool 9 fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Slow: Try light tackle and small plastic baits in the flooded timber as the river rises.
Smallmouth Bass – Excellent: Smallmouth are biting in areas with moderate current. Cast spinners and crankbaits along the main channel rock shorelines.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Pleasant Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black Crappie – Fair: Find crappie in 10-15 feet of water along trees and breaks.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Rathbun Reservoir fishing report
reports.text: Black Crappie – Slow: Some anglers are using jigs around submerged cedar tree piles and docks.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Red Rock Reservoir fishing report
reports.text: White Crappie – Good: Crappies have moved shallow. Use live minnows or plastics near any rock riprap or wood in 2 to 6 feet of water.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Rodgers Park Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Fair.
Largemouth Bass – Fair.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Silver Lake (Worth) fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth Bass – Good: Slow retrieved bass baits work best with the current cooler water temperatures.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Spirit Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black Crappie – Good: Anglers are finding quality-size fish.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Turkey River (above Clermont) fishing report
reports.text: Smallmouth Bass – Fair: Find smallies in back eddies or along current breaks.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Twelve Mile Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black Crappie – Fair: Try jigs or twister tails along rocky shoreline areas to catch all sizes of crappie.
Largemouth Bass – Fair: Catch largemouth bass up to 19-inches with jigs or finesse plastics along rocky shorelines.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Upper Iowa River (above Decorah) fishing report
reports.text: Smallmouth Bass – Fair: Anglers are catching 10- to 12-inch bass below dams with live bait.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Volga Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black Crappie – Fair: Find crappie near rocky shoreline or around woody habitat.

reports.source: Iowa DNR weekly fishing report (KCHA News)
reports.title: Wapsipinicon River (Tripoli to Troy Mills) fishing report
reports.text:
Reports of anglers catching smallmouth bass and walleyes.
Smallmouth Bass – Fair: Cast and retrieve lead head jigs tipped with plastics and a minnow.
